idiom_name: Slick TableQuery[Orders] with filter/map and Seq results
implementation_notes: Slick lifts the table into a first-class value: a Table class plus TableQuery[Orders] is the module, and its combinators (filter, map, groupBy, sortBy) are the set-oriented operations, with .result turning a query into an Action that db.run executes into Seq[OrderRow] - the sequence is the record set. Rules that act on the whole table are functions taking the TableQuery and returning another query or a Seq, and the row type stays a plain record so no per-row behaviour accumulates. Use Slick's combinators rather than Scala collection methods on a fetched Seq whenever the rule can be expressed in SQL.
pitfalls: db.run returns Future/IO: composing several queries without .transactionally (or an explicit transaction) interleaves them with other work and loses atomicity.

Lifted columns are Rep[T] rather than T, so == instead of === can compile for some types and generate the wrong predicate, and a monadic join Slick cannot translate fails at runtime - keep set-shaped rules in applicative style.
